Metadata.description: Steve Diego builds fast websites and web apps with Next.js, Laravel and Django. Based in Douala, Cameroon. See recent projects and get a quote.
Metadata.keywords: full-stack developer, web developer, Next.js, Laravel, Django, TypeScript, React, TailwindCSS, GSAP, Douala, Cameroon, freelance developer, web application, website development, performance, accessibility
Metadata.author: Steve Diego TAKOUDJOU

Hero.description1: I design and build websites and web apps with Next.js, Laravel and Django. One person handles the sketch, the code and the launch, so nothing gets lost between a designer and a developer.
Hero.description2: Three years of full-stack work, including a carpooling platform, a hoodie store and an AI tool that writes software specs. Based in Douala, working with clients anywhere.

About.title: About Me
About.description: I care how a site looks, how fast it loads, and whether it still works on a phone with two bars of signal. All three get checked before launch.

item1.description: One codebase, one person to call. I build the API, the database and the interface. When something breaks, the person who fixes it is the person who built it.

item2.description: Code the next developer can read. Typed, documented and organised by feature, so adding a page in year two costs about what it cost in week two.

item3.description: Speed handled during the build. Images, fonts and scripts get sized and deferred before launch, so the site stays quick on a mid-range phone.

item4.description: You keep everything at the end. Domain, hosting, source code and accounts go to you, with a walkthrough of how to update the content yourself.

Projects.title: Projects
Projects.description: Five recent builds: a fashion studio, a hotel, an enrolment manager, a hoodie store and an AI tool for software specs. Open any of them.
Projects.demoNote: Demo account for reviewing the dashboard. Please don't change or delete existing records.

fashionStudio.description: A stark black-and-white storefront for a fashion studio. Editorial layouts, oversized type and a product grid that keeps the clothes, not the interface, in charge. Built to feel like a lookbook, with fast image loading and a checkout flow that stays out of the way.

odysiaHotel.description: A booking-first site for a boutique hotel. Warm photography, a room finder and a clear path from browsing to reservation, with the details travellers actually need before they book.

mdsEnrollment.description: A back-office tool for managing student enrolment. Staff look up applicants, confirm registrations and keep records current from one dashboard, instead of a shared spreadsheet that two people cannot safely edit at once.

buildocs.description: An AI-assisted workspace for software teams that turns rough product ideas into structured specs. Draft, review and hand off requirements without losing the decisions along the way.

hoodiego.description: A small-batch hoodie store with a bold orange identity. Product pages, size selection and a checkout flow built for a store that sells a few things well rather than everything at once.

item1.quote: He took the carpooling idea from a rough sketch to a working platform, front end and back end, faster than we expected. The dashboard is the part our drivers keep mentioning.

item2.quote: We asked for a spec tool and got something our project managers use every week. Steve explained the AI side in plain language and left notes on how to run it.

Contact.title: Contact Me

Contact.description1: For project enquiries and quotes. I reply within one working day.
Contact.description2: Based in Douala. Most work happens over email and video calls.

CTA.title: Most customers meet your website before they meet you.

FAQ.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.description: What clients usually ask before we start. Open any question, or email me if yours isn't here.
FAQ.paragraph: Can't find what you're looking for?

item1.question: What services do you offer?
item1.answer: Custom websites, full-stack web apps, performance work on an existing site, and the hosting setup to get it online. Next.js and TypeScript on the front end, Laravel or Django on the back end.

item2.question: How long does it take to build a website?
item2.answer: A five-page marketing site takes one to two weeks. A web app with accounts, a database and a dashboard takes four to eight weeks. You get a date before we start, and I tell you early if it moves.

item3.question: Do you provide ongoing support?
item3.answer: Yes. Monthly maintenance covers updates, backups, security patches and small changes. You can also take the code and run it yourself; I'll walk you through the handover.

item4.question: What is your pricing structure?
item4.answer: A fixed price per project, agreed in writing before work starts. Apps are quoted after a short scoping call, so the number you get is the number you pay.

item5.question: What payment methods do you accept?
item5.answer: PayPal, Orange Money and MTN Mobile Money. For larger projects we agree a payment schedule before the first line of code.

item6.question: Can you handle hosting?
item6.answer: Yes. I buy the domain, set up hosting and deploy the site, then hand you the login details. You keep ownership of the domain and every account.
